transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess the main thing bringing me in is that I just keep getting pulled off track by every little sound or thought. 

Like, I’ll be trying to sit down and work on a job application, and then... I don't know, a car goes by outside, or my phone lights up, or I just get some random idea in my head. It just sends me somewhere completely different, and I'm off doing something else before I even notice I stopped working on the application in the first place. It's just making it really hard to get anything done.
Can you tell me whether this kind of distractibility has been a pattern for you since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently, like in the past several months?

It's definitely not a recent thing. It's, um, it's been a pattern since I was a kid. Even back in elementary school, I remember teachers were always moving my seat around because I'd talk out of turn. I was always forgetting my homework, too. And when I did sit down to do the work, I'd just rush through the worksheets and make all these careless mistakes. So, yeah, it's pretty much always been like this.
Do you often feel restless, feel the need to be constantly moving, or find yourself interrupting others or acting impulsively without thinking things through?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I used to play a lot of soccer, which helped, but since I can't really do that like I used to, sitting around the house just... it makes me feel like I'm crawling out of my skin. I just can't settle down. I usually end up just pacing from room to room because I feel like I have to be moving.
Do these difficulties with focus and restlessness cause problems for you in more than one area of your life—for example, both at work and in your personal relationships or home life?

Yeah, it definitely does. It affects a lot of things. Like, I've been trying to get a career going as an automotive technician. I know for a fact I can handle the hands-on work part of it—I'm good at that. But... well, sitting at home trying to get the paperwork done is a disaster. I've missed training deadlines, and I've had to redo applications so many times because I just can't focus or sit still long enough to finish them right. So I'm still not moving forward with it at all. It just stops me from actually getting my life together.

Have you ever had distinct periods lasting several days or more where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, or felt like your thoughts were racing much more than your usual baseline?

No, I don't think so. I mean, my thoughts are always kind of jumping around, like I said, but it's pretty much the same all the time. I've never had a time where I felt super high or didn't need to sleep for days or anything like that. It's just my normal everyday restless feeling, not some big change that lasts for a few days.
